chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Striving (ijtihad) would not benefit if there is no devoutness (war') in it.

key_terms.اجْتِهَادٌ: Striving or intellectual effort, often referring to independent legal reasoning or deep religious study.
key_terms.وَرَاعَ: Devoutness, piety, or God-consciousness; a state of guarding oneself against sin through awareness of God.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between ijtihad and war' (piety) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), establishing a critical criterion for the validity of ijtihad in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores that intellectual rigor alone is insufficient; without wara' (piety and God-consciousness), scholarly effort fails to yield spiritual benefit or accurate religious understanding. This hadith serves as a foundational reminder that moral integrity is the vessel through which knowledge becomes transformative.
